MCPCOMPANION.SettingTelemetryHint: Report your token selections, targets and viewed scene to the MCP server (per-client). Turn off to keep this client private.
MCPCOMPANION.SettingRunScriptHint: Lets a connected MCP client run arbitrary JavaScript in this browser with your Gamemaster rights: read and alter every document, act as you, reach anything your session reaches. That code is often written by an AI model and nobody reviews it before it runs. Every execution is printed in full to the browser console (F12) in all modes, so you can audit what ran. Leave it disabled unless you trust every client holding your gateway secret.
MCPCOMPANION.RunScriptConfirm: Ask me first — show the code and wait for my approval
MCPCOMPANION.RunScriptAuto: Run automatically — no prompt, console log only
MCPCOMPANION.RunScriptConfirmBody: A connected MCP client is asking to run this code with your Gamemaster rights. Read it before approving — declining is safe, the client is simply told no.
MCPCOMPANION.SettingRunMacroHint: Controls what happens when a connected MCP client asks to run one of your macros of type "script" — which is JavaScript running with your Gamemaster rights, just like remote script execution above. Macros of type "chat" are never affected, and neither is anything you launch yourself from the Foundry interface: this only covers macros driven by an MCP client.
MCPCOMPANION.RunMacroConfirmBody: A connected MCP client is asking to run your script macro "{name}" with your Gamemaster rights. Read it before approving — declining is safe, the client is simply told no.
MCPCOMPANION.SettingRootKeyHint: The public key of the gateway allowed to drive this world. Commands not signed by it are refused. Get it with `foundry-mcp --print-public-key`, or let the gateway install it itself with its companion_trust_key tool. Left empty, commands that execute code (scripts, script macros) stop working — everything else keeps running.
MCPCOMPANION.SettingVerifyHint: Foundry relays module socket channels to every connected client and never says who sent a message, so without a signature any player could ask your browser to run a command with your Gamemaster rights. Leave this on Guarded unless you have a reason not to.
MCPCOMPANION.ErrNoKey: No gateway public key is configured in this world, so this command cannot be authenticated. Run the companion_trust_key tool from your MCP client, or paste the key from `foundry-mcp --print-public-key` into this module's settings.
MCPCOMPANION.ErrBadSignature: Command signature rejected — it was not sent by the trusted gateway.
MCPCOMPANION.ErrBadKey: The gateway public key configured in this world is not readable. Check it in this module's settings.
MCPCOMPANION.ErrClockSkew: Command expired. If this keeps happening, check the clock on the machine running this browser.
MCPCOMPANION.ErrWrongWorld: This command was signed for a different world.
MCPCOMPANION.WarnKeyChanged: The gateway public key changed during this session. The previous key stays in force until you reload. If you did not do this, someone else can modify your world settings.
MCPCOMPANION.WarnSettingsPermission: In this world, a role below Assistant can modify world settings — including this module's trusted gateway key. Review Configure Permissions → Modify World Settings.
